security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Go struct tags, Markdown code fences, local documentation URLs, and standard template configuration. Real concerns remain around direct shell-command execution with user-controlled placeholders and a Python config path that can print a password-bearing database URI.

remediation.issue: Direct execution guidance for scaffold commands
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running package managers, dev servers, or shell scripts. Validate project names and target directories before interpolation.
Use safe argument arrays or validated identifiers instead of interpolating project names and paths into sed, cd, and find commands.
Remove the config.py __main__ print path or mask the password before printing any database URI.
Document all network-based installs and let users approve npm, uv, go, npx, and remote theme fetches before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Database URI Secret Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The Python backend configuration can print settings.DataBaseURI when config.py is run as a script. That URI is built with POSTGRES_PASSWORD and can expose database credentials in terminal logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URI builder includes POSTGRES_PASSWORD and the module prints the resulting DataBaseURI in both the template and reference guide. Exposure requires manual execution, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Starting a modern app requires many repeated setup steps. Genesis provides templates and reference guides for React, FastAPI, Go Gin, Taro, landing pages, and motion.
actual_capabilities: Scaffold a React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS V4, and shadcn/ui frontend starter.
Scaffold a FastAPI backend with UV, SQLModel, AsyncPG, settings, and sample routers.
Scaffold a Go Gin backend with GORM, Viper, middleware, DTOs, and config files.
Scaffold a Taro 4 miniapp with React, Tailwind CSS, and multi-platform scripts.
Guide landing page generation, design system setup, and Framer Motion enhancements.
limitations: Some source guidance is written in Chinese and may require translation for all teams.
Template setup can run package managers and local development servers.
Generated projects still need app-specific security, authentication, and deployment hardening.
Database and environment settings must be reviewed before real deployment.

use_cases.title: Start a React product interface
use_cases.description: Create a Vite and Tailwind frontend with shadcn/ui conventions ready for product screens.

use_cases.title: Create a backend service baseline
use_cases.description: Generate a FastAPI or Go Gin service with standard folders, configuration, routing, and database wiring.

use_cases.title: Prototype a cross-platform app
use_cases.description: Create a Taro miniapp starter or landing page for rapid validation across channels.

prompt_templates.title: Create a React starter
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Genesis to create a React project named customer-portal in ./apps/customer-portal. Ask me for the initialization mode before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Create a FastAPI service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Genesis to create a FastAPI backend named billing-api. Show the planned files and commands before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Taro miniapp
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Genesis to create a Taro miniapp named loyalty-miniapp. Configure it for WeChat first and list platform scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Build a complete prototype
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Genesis references to create a React landing page and matching Go Gin API. Confirm directories, commands, and dependencies before running setup.

output_examples.input: Create a React project called studio-dashboard.
output_examples.output: Genesis asks for the setup mode, confirms the target folder, then creates a Vite React starter with Tailwind and shadcn/ui.

output_examples.input: Create a Python backend for user profiles.
output_examples.output: Genesis prepares a FastAPI service with configuration, database session wiring, routers, schemas, and a local run script.

output_examples.input: Generate a landing page for my new analytics product.
output_examples.output: Genesis applies the landing page guide to produce structured sections, responsive layout guidance, and motion recommendations.

best_practices: Confirm the target directory and project name before any scaffold command runs.
Review package manager commands before installing dependencies from public registries.
Replace example environment values and keep local .env files out of source control.
anti_patterns: Do not run template command blocks without reviewing the target path.
Do not use starter database settings in shared or production environments.
Do not merge generated routes into an existing app without reviewing conflicts.

faq.question: What project types can Genesis create?
faq.answer: It supports React frontends, FastAPI backends, Go Gin backends, Taro miniapps, landing pages, and React motion upgrades.

faq.question: Does it use templates or generate files from instructions?
faq.answer: It supports both. Template copy is faster, while AI generation uses reference guides for deeper customization.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: The skill includes commands for npm, uv, go, and npx. Review and approve those commands before execution.

faq.question: Is it production ready?
faq.answer: It creates strong starter structures. You still need security review, real credentials, deployment settings, and product-specific logic.

faq.question: What should I check after scaffolding?
faq.answer: Check generated names, routes, environment files, package scripts, database settings, and local server behavior.
